title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.29): M is a set (abstract 'multiplicities' or points of a stratified object). F_M is a set of 'M-figures', each figure Φ ⊂ P(M) being a set of strata. M* = ∪_{Φ∈F_M} Φ. Axiom Ax*1 says M* is itself a figure with support M, and that the associated preorder ≪ on M is a partial order. Hence the 'shadow' map (*) x ↦ M_{≪x} = Omb(x) is a bijection M → M* that turns ≪ into inclusion. The elements of M* are exactly the irreducible closed subsets of M that have a generic point, i.e. M with its Alexandrov topology is sober/T0.

This page:
(1) Every figure Φ satisfies Φ ⊂ M*, so Φ is the image under (*) of a unique subset F ⊂ M, namely Φ = F̃ = {M_{≪x} | x ∈ F}. Through ≪, the family F_M ⊂ P(P(M)) is therefore identified with a family F̃ ⊂ P(M) of subsets of the poset (M, ≪).
(2) Grothendieck then wants to characterise which families F̃ arise. These are the ones satisfying conditions C1, C2, C3 from an earlier chapter ('CF IV', pp. 54, 55, 58), for which the incidence relation is identified with inclusion of strata.
(3) The key condition is 'preadmissibility': for every x ∈ M there is a smallest member of F̃ containing x. Restated as Ax*2: for Φ ∈ F_M and A = Omb(x) ∈ Φ, there is a smallest figure Φ_A ∈ F_M having A as an element; by minimality Φ_A ⊂ Φ. The margin calls Φ_A 'the multiplicity (multistrate) of the figure A'.
(4) Ax*3: if Φ_i ∈ F_M are all contained in some Φ ∈ F_M, then ∪Φ_i ∈ F_M (stability under bounded unions; the bottom note says 'this is C1 for F_M').

The next page completes the picture. ∅ ∈ F_M (empty bounded union). Ax*4 is a binary-coherence axiom: Φ ∪ Ψ ∈ F_M iff Φ_A ∪ Ψ_B ∈ F_M for all A ∈ Φ, B ∈ Ψ. Φ_A is shown to be the set of substrata of A in Φ and to be independent of Φ, so figures are down-closed and Φ ⊂ Ψ implies Φ is closed in Ψ.

In modern terms: (M, ≪) is a poset, i.e. a T0 Alexandrov space. Figures are down-closed subsets of M that contain the principal down-set ↓x of each of their points (Φ_A ↔ ↓x). The family is closed under bounded unions and under pairwise-coherent unions. Purpose: an intrinsic, purely combinatorial axiomatics of the 'figures' (closed unions of strata, subcomplexes) of a tame stratified space, in the 1986 Analysis situs programme.
errors: No mathematical error found. Φ_A ⊂ Φ follows from minimality since A ∈ Φ, and ∅ ∈ F_M follows from Ax*3 applied to the empty family (as the next page notes).
Preadmissibility is stated first for F̃ in terms of points x and then for F_M in terms of strata A; the two agree only via the bijection (*), which relies on Ax*1. This is implicit but correct.
That Φ_A equals the full set of substrata of A (so that figures are down-closed) is only established on the next page; on this page it is not yet justified.

ideas.what: Identification of strata with principal down-sets (shadows Omb(x) = M_{≪x}) and of figures with subsets of the poset M
ideas.modern_name: Alexandrov topology / specialization order of a finite T0 (sober) space; face poset of a stratification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937), McCord and Stong (1966) for finite spaces
ideas.where_published: Generic points/sobriety appear in EGA I (0.2.1); this specific use is unpublished

ideas.what: Preadmissibility: each stratum A lies in a smallest figure Φ_A (its 'multistrate'), independent of the ambient figure
ideas.modern_name: closed cell / closure star of a stratum; prime element [e] (principal down-set) in a family of configurations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cell-complex tradition; for the abstract version Nielsen-Plotkin-Winskel (1981)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only sketches 'tame topology' without these axioms

ideas.what: Axioms on the set of figures: down-closure, bounded unions (Ax*3), ∅, and binary coherence of unions (Ax*4, next page)
ideas.modern_name: configurations of a prime event structure with binary conflict; prime-algebraic coherent domains (dI-domains); coherence-space-like structures

missed.claim: Grothendieck's intrinsic axioms for the family of 'figures' of a stratified space coincide formally with the axioms for configurations of a prime event structure, i.e. prime-algebraic coherent domains (Nielsen-Plotkin-Winskel). In that dictionary, strata/points are events, ≪ is causality, Φ_A = Omb-down-set is the prime [e], bounded unions are consistent joins, and Ax*4 is binary conflict/coherence. He reached this independently in 1986 from geometry, at the same time as the theoretical computer science development. No link between tame stratified topology axiomatics and event-structure/domain theory appears in the literature.
missed.quote: il existe une plus petite figure Φ_A ∈ F_M ... At*3. Si Φ ∈ F_M, et si Φ_i ∈ F_M, Φ_i ⊂ Φ, alors ∪Φ_i ∈ F_M (stabilité par réunions majorées dans F_M)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Directed/concurrency topology (Fajstrup, Goubault, Raussen; Gaucher) already links event structures to stratified and directed spaces. Grothendieck's axioms could give a geometric, intrinsic definition of such spaces, and conversely bring domain-theoretic tools to tame/o-minimal stratifications and exit-path categories.

missed.claim: The programme of characterising intrinsically which set-systems F̃ ⊂ P(M) arise as the figures of a tame stratified space (the C1–C3 plus Ax*1–Ax*4 axiomatics) is an unpublished axiomatisation of 'tame topology' at the combinatorial level.
missed.quote: Ainsi, on peut aussi interpréter, grâce à ≪, F_M en termes d'un ensemble de parties F̃ de M
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Relevant to combinatorial models of conically stratified spaces (exit-path ∞-categories, Lurie/Ayala-Francis-Tanaka) and to o-minimal 'tame topology', which Grothendieck called for in the Esquisse.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a routine reformulation (figures as subsets of a poset, minimal figures, bounded unions). Together with the next page's coherence axiom, however, it reproduces the event-structure/coherent-domain axioms, an unremarked parallel with computer science. It is a formal coincidence rather than a deep theorem, hence modest surprise.
transcription_corrections: 'l'image de (1.79) 30 (as)' is more likely 'l'image par (*)' (the map (*) from p.29), with '1.79' crossed out and '30' as the page number.
The crossed-out symbol in Φ = {… | X ∈ F} is Omb(x), with 'M_{≪x}' written underneath; read Φ = {Omb(x) | x ∈ F}.
'At*2', 'At*3' should be 'Ax*2', 'Ax*3' (the next page has 'Af*' for the same).
'ceux que satisfont' should be 'ceux qui satisfont'.
Margin 'CF IV' likely means 'cf. Ch. IV' (chapter IV, pp. 54-55, 58).
Margin 'c'est la multiplicité de figure A' could be read 'c'est la multistrate de figure A' (consistent with 'multistrates' on the next page).
